words.sense: win agreement through flattery and persistent gentle persuasion
misconceptions: Friendly repetition must mean an actual threat

words.sense: compel someone through threatened harm, force or intimidation
misconceptions: A charming tone cancels any threat attached to the demand

semantic_axes.description: Flattery and patient coaxing differ from imposing compliance through threats or force.

edges.boundary_rule: cajole persuades by coaxing or flattery; coerce compels through threat, intimidation or force.
clues_b: uses control to remove a choice

misconceptions.M1: Assumes persistence is the same as a threat
misconceptions.M2: Assumes a friendly tone makes a threat harmless
misconceptions.M3: Confuses offers or praise with penalties for refusal

chains.frame: Which word best describes Amina's effort to get help with her slides?

beats.text: Amina praised her classmate's design skills and kept asking if he would help polish the slides.
beats.decisive_clue: flattery and repeated requests without a threat
beats.reason: She is trying to win agreement through praise.

beats.text: She then said she would delete his finished work from the shared folder unless he agreed.
beats.decisive_clue: threatened destruction of his work for refusal
beats.reason: A threatened penalty turns this into compulsion, not merely friendly coaxing.

chains.feedback_short: The new fact changes the answer: threatened destruction of his work for refusal.
chains.feedback_deep: Cajole means to coax or flatter someone into doing something; coerce means to pressure someone into compliance through force or threats. She is trying to win agreement through praise. A threatened penalty turns this into compulsion, not merely friendly coaxing.
chains.contrast_rule: cajole persuades by coaxing or flattery; coerce compels through threat, intimidation or force.
